shipped.kurz: The old decretals: Exiit qui seminat (1279) and Exivi de paradiso (1312)
shipped.warum: What the dispute was about, from Friedberg's Corpus iuris canonici, Latin with a working translation, in excerpts: Nicholas III declares renunciation of ownership 'not only individually but also in common' the way of Christ, explains Christ's purse as condescension to the weak, and distinguishes property, possession, usufruct, the right of using and the 'simple use of fact'; the Roman Church takes the ownership; no one may gloss it. Clement V at Vienne hears the Spirituals' list of the Community's excesses and rules on granaries and 'poor use'.

shipped.kurz: The pope's dossier: the decretals of John XXII
shipped.warum: Five decretals on 'the meaning of words', from Friedberg's Corpus iuris canonici, Latin with a working translation: obedience above poverty (1317); the question opened (1322); the Roman Church renounces its 'verbal, bare and enigmatic' ownership of the friars' goods, since no one can use an egg without owning it (1322); the assertion that Christ had nothing 'nor even in common' declared heretical (1323); the friars' 'key of knowledge' called a doctrine of the father of lies (1324).

planned.warum: The order's answer to the pope's question: that Christ and the apostles had nothing by right of property or ownership, individually or in common. The words John XXII condemned.
planned.quelle: Printed text to be identified among the public-domain editions (Wadding, Annales Minorum; Baluze, Miscellanea).

planned.kurz: The order's chronicle: Michael of Cesena
planned.warum: How the order remembered its general: his election, Perugia, the summons to Avignon, the flight, the deposition.
planned.quelle: Chronica XXIV Generalium Ordinis Minorum, in Analecta Franciscana III (Quaracchi 1897).

planned.warum: The general's case against the pope, after the flight: the heretic is John XXII.
planned.quelle: Baluze, Miscellanea, ed. Mansi, vol. III (Lucca 1762).

planned.warum: Louis the Bavarian's appeal against the pope, with its long passage on the poverty of Christ written by Franciscans: the dispute becomes imperial politics.
planned.quelle: MGH, Constitutiones V (1909–13). Rights to be checked.

planned.warum: The answer to Ad conditorem and Quia vir reprobus, point by point, from exile in Munich: use, right, ownership, and what an act is.
planned.quelle: Goldast, Monarchia S. Romani Imperii II (Frankfurt 1614). Excerpts.

planned.kurz: The Book of Sentences of the inquisition of Toulouse
planned.warum: Bernard Gui's sentences, 1307–1323, among them the Beguins who held that the pope could not change the rule of Francis: each by name, place, belief and penalty. The game's list of the burned will be taken from here and link to each sentence.
planned.quelle: Liber sententiarum inquisitionis Tholosanae, in Philipp van Limborch, Historia inquisitionis (Amsterdam 1692), vol. II. Internet Archive. Public domain.

planned.warum: The inquisitor of Toulouse on the Beguins of Provence: what they believed about poverty, how they were questioned, how they died.
planned.quelle: Bernard Gui, Practica inquisitionis heretice pravitatis, ed. C. Douais (Paris 1886).

planned.warum: The Spirituals' own history of the order as a history of persecution.
planned.quelle: Historia septem tribulationum, ed. F. Ehrle, Archiv für Litteratur- und Kirchengeschichte II (1886).

planned.kurz: Dante, Paradiso XI: Francis and Lady Poverty
planned.warum: Written in the same years (c. 1316–1321): Thomas Aquinas praises Francis, who married Poverty, 'widowed' since Christ, and laments the Dominicans; Italian with Longfellow's translation.
planned.quelle: Dante, Paradiso XI; H. W. Longfellow, The Divine Comedy (Boston 1867).
